questions.question: If 21 July 1999 was Wednesday, then what day was it on 21 November 1999?
questions.solution:
Given: 21 July 1999 was a Wednesday.

Target Date: 21 November 1999.

Calculating the total number of days from 21 July 1999 to 21 November 1999:

Days remaining in July: 31 − 21 = 10 days

Days in August: 31 days

Days in September: 30 days

Days in October: 31 days

Days in November: 21 days (up to the 21st)

Total number of days = 10 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 21 = 123 days

To find the number of odd days, we divide the total number of days by 7:

123 ÷ 7 = 17 weeks and 4 days remainder.

So, there are 4 odd days.

Now, count 4 days forward from Wednesday:

1 day after Wednesday = Thursday

2 days after Wednesday = Friday

3 days after Wednesday = Saturday

4 days after Wednesday = Sunday

Therefore, the day on 21 November 1999 was Sunday.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: Who has the power to recommend President's Rule in a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** of a state has the constitutional authority under **Article 356** of the **Indian Constitution** to recommend the imposition of **President’s Rule** (also known as State Emergency).
 
• This recommendation is made when the **Governor** is satisfied that the government of the state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the **Constitution**, signifying a breakdown of constitutional machinery.
 
• While the **President** is the authority who officially issues the proclamation, they generally act based on a formal report submitted by the **Governor**, though the President can also act independently if a grave situation arises.
 
• Upon the imposition of **President’s Rule**, the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister** is dismissed, and the state administration comes under the direct control of the **Union Government** through the **Governor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework**:

 
 
• **Article 356**: Inspired by **Section 93** of the **Government of India Act, 1935**, it allows the Center to take over state administration.
 
• **Parliamentary Approval**: Every proclamation of **President’s Rule** must be approved by both houses of **Parliament** within **two months** (60 days) by a **simple majority**.
 
• **Duration**: Once approved, it continues for **six months** and can be extended up to a maximum of **three years** with periodic parliamentary approval every six months.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Oversight**:
 
 
• **S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)**: A landmark **Supreme Court** judgement that established the power of **judicial review** over the President’s proclamation to prevent the arbitrary dismissal of state governments.
 
• The court ruled that the **floor test** in the **State Legislative Assembly** is the only valid way to check the majority of a government.
 
 
 
• **Related Emergency Provisions**:
 
 
• **Article 352**: Relates to **National Emergency** due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• **Article 360**: Relates to **Financial Emergency**, which has never been declared in India to date.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority in the State Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 164** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Chief Minister** is appointed by the **Governor** of the state.
 
• While the Governor normally appoints the leader of the party that secures a majority in the **State Legislative Assembly**, they exercise **situational discretion** when no single party or alliance has a clear majority.
 
• In the event of a **hung assembly**, the Governor is responsible for appointing a person who is most likely to command the **confidence of the house** to ensure a stable government.
 
• The Governor generally invites the leader of the **single largest party** or a **post-poll alliance** to form the ministry and prove their majority on the floor of the house through a **vote of confidence**.
 
• This discretionary power is a vital constitutional function meant to prevent a **constitutional breakdown** or political instability within the state executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• The **President of India** appoints the **Prime Minister** under **Article 75** but does not have the authority to appoint a State Chief Minister.
 
• The President acts as the **nominal head** of the Union, whereas the Governor acts as the nominal head of the state.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Assembly**:
 
 
• The **Speaker** is the **presiding officer** of the **Vidhan Sabha**, elected by its members.
 
• The Speaker’s role is limited to legislative proceedings and maintaining house decorum; they hold no executive power to appoint the **Chief Minister**.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the real executive head of the **Union Government**.
 
• While the PM may influence political decisions through the party hierarchy, the **Constitution** does not grant the PM any formal power in the appointment process of a **Chief Minister**.

__
 
• To study the **history of Indian music**, one must trace back to the **human origin**, as music is intrinsically linked to the biological and psychological development of mankind.
 
• The fundamental element of music is **Nada (Sound)**; ancient Indian musicology identifies it as the primordial vibration from which the universe emerged, often termed **Nada Brahma**.
 
• **Swar (Tone)** is the melodic foundation that differentiates musical sound from noise; historical study begins with how humans transitioned from **monotone vocalizations** to the structured **Sama Veda** chants.
 
• **Laya (Rhythm)** represents the temporal aspect of music, derived from natural phenomena like the **heartbeat** or the **seasons**, which provided the first rhythmic frameworks for early humans.
 
• Understanding these three pillars (**Sound, Tone, and Rhythm**) is essential before analyzing the complex **Raga-Tala** systems found in texts like the **Natya Shastra** by **Bharat Muni**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Analysis of Related Concepts**:

 
 
• **Human Evolution and Technical Skills**: While **technical skills** are necessary for instrument making, they are considered secondary developments that occurred after the realization of vocal **tone** and **rhythm**.
 
• **Civilization and Language**: **Language** is a medium of literal communication, whereas music is a **universal language of sound** that existed prior to the formalization of scripts and complex grammars.
 
• **Instruments and Dance**: In the classical definition of **Sangeetam** (Gitam Vadyam tatha Nrityam), **Gitam** (vocal/sound) is the primary element that directs the **Vadyam** (instruments) and **Nrityam** (dance).
 
 
 
• **Historical Foundations**:
 
 
• **Shruti**: The history of Indian music relies on the **22 Shrutis** (microtones), which are the smallest audible frequencies perceived by the human ear.
 
• **Vedic Music**: The transition from **Archik** (one note) and **Gathik** (two notes) to **Samik** (three notes) represents the earliest **tonal history** of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: The Malwa Plateau is primarily located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Malwa Plateau** is a prominent physiographic division of India located in the **west-central** part of the country, primarily occupying the western region of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Geologically, the plateau is of **volcanic origin** and forms a part of the **Deccan Traps**, which were created by **fissure eruptions** of basaltic lava during the **Cretaceous period**.
 
• The region is bounded by the **Vindhya Range** to the south and the **Madhya Bharat Pathar** and **Bundelkhand** to the north and northeast, serving as a transitional landform between the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** and the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• The plateau is characterized by a **rolling surface** with an average elevation ranging between **500 to 600 meters** above sea level, sloping generally towards the **north** and **northeast**.
 
• The drainage system of the plateau includes major rivers such as the **Chambal**, **Kali Sindh**, **Shipra**, **Parbati**, and **Betwa**, all of which eventually join the **Yamuna** or the **Ganga**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil and Agriculture:**

 
 
• The plateau is covered with fertile **Black Soil** (also known as **Regur soil**), which is highly moisture-retentive and rich in **iron** and **magnesium**.
 
• This soil type makes the region a hub for the production of **Soybean**, **Wheat**, **Cotton**, and **Gram**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Extensions:**
 
 
• **Rajasthan:** While primarily in Madhya Pradesh, the southeastern portion of Rajasthan, known as the **Hadoti region** (including Kota, Bundi, and Jhalawar), is a part of this plateau system.
 
• **Gujarat and Maharashtra:** These states share boundaries with the plateau region but do not house the primary expanse of the **Malwa** landform itself.
 
 
 
• **Climate:** The region experiences a **tropical climate** with moderate temperatures, largely influenced by its inland location and elevation.

questions.question: The Bhabar zone is associated with which physiographic feature of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himalayan foothills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhabar** is a narrow belt ranging between **8 to 16 km** in width, lying parallel to the **Shiwalik foothills** at the break-of-slope.
 
• It is the northernmost stretch of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, forming the transition zone where the **Himalayan rivers** descend from the mountains and deposit heavy materials.
 
• The region is characterized by the accumulation of **pebbles**, gravel, and rock debris, making the soil structure extremely porous.
 
• Due to this high **porosity**, smaller **rivers and streams disappear** underground in this zone, flowing beneath the surface of the pebble-studded bed.
 
• The **Bhabar** belt extends from the **Indus** river in the west to the **Teesta** river in the east, marking the edge of the **extra-peninsular** mountain system.

questions.question: When nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rises faster than real GDP, it indicates:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High inflation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures the total value of all goods and services produced within a country at **current market prices**, meaning it accounts for both changes in production volume and changes in prices.
 
• **Real GDP** measures the economic output adjusted for price changes (inflation or deflation) by using **constant prices** from a designated **base year**, providing a clearer picture of actual production growth.
 
• The divergence between these two metrics is captured by the **GDP Deflator**, a price index calculated as ({Nominal GDP} / {Real GDP}) times 100 , which serves as a broad measure of **inflation**.
 
• When **Nominal GDP** rises faster than **Real GDP**, the growth in the nominal figure is not solely due to increased output but is heavily influenced by a significant rise in the **general price level**.
 
• This scenario directly indicates **High inflation**, as the cost of goods and services is increasing rapidly, causing the nominal value of the economy to swell even if the physical quantity of goods produced remains relatively stable or grows slowly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation and Deflation**:

 
 
• **Deflation**: Characterized by a general decline in prices; in this case, **Real GDP** growth would typically exceed **Nominal GDP** growth.
 
• **Falling Inflation**: Often called **disinflation**, this refers to a reduction in the rate at which prices increase, rather than a total decline in price levels.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth Metrics**:
 
 
• **Zero Growth**: A state where the **Real GDP** remains constant over time, indicating no improvement in the country's productive capacity or standard of living.
 
• **Purchasing Power**: During periods of high inflation, the **purchasing power** of the domestic currency declines, requiring more money to buy the same amount of goods as in the previous year.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 cm.**

⇒ Side a = √(12² + 16²)

⇒ Side a = √(144 + 256) = √400

⇒ Side a = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 80 cm.**

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 20. Least Common Multiple of C and D is 30. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B, C and D?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** follows the **associative property**, which states that LCM(A, B, C, D) = LCM[LCM(A, B), LCM(C, D)].

⇒ Given LCM(A, B) = 20 and LCM(C, D) = 30.

⇒ Required LCM = LCM(20, 30).

⇒ The smallest number divisible by both 20 and 30 is 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of A and B = 20

LCM of C and D = 30

**Formula Used:**

LCM(a, b, c, d) = LCM(LCM(a, b), LCM(c, d))

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33f6458cafa37d89f0206f2e76b7ecc378829687d7ee56fbacdc68d4ba53ce37.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ We need to find the **LCM of 20 and 30**.

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 = 2² × 5

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM is the product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors involved.

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Associative Property of LCM

The LCM of a set of numbers can be found by grouping them: LCM(a, b, c) = LCM(a, LCM(b, c)).

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of (a/b, c/d) = LCM of numerators (a, c) ÷ HCF of denominators (b, d).

questions.question: The Least Common Multiple of two numbers is 90. Which of the following can be the Highest Common Factor of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of any set of numbers is always a **factor** of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Given **LCM** = 90, the potential **HCF** must divide 90 exactly without a remainder.

Checking options: 90 ÷ 28 (No) | 90 ÷ 24 (No) | 90 ÷ 36 (No) | 90 ÷ 15 = 6 (Yes).

Since only 15 is a **factor** of 90, it is the only possible **HCF**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**LCM** of two numbers = 90

**Formula/Property:**

For any two integers, **LCM** = **HCF** × k (where k is a positive integer representing the product of the non-common prime factors).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c7b2288e8f485bf17c61cbdfeed7e25bd9ed4829b58eadd68dff0c7f5210377.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **HCF** be 'h'. Then 90/h must be an integer.

⇒ Option 1: 90 ÷ 28 ≈ 3.21 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 2: 90 ÷ 24 = 3.75 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 3: 90 ÷ 36 = 2.5 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 4: 90 ÷ 15 = 6 (Integer)

⇒ Since 15 divides 90 perfectly, it can be the **HCF**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two positive integers a and b: Product of numbers = **HCF**(a, b) × **LCM**(a, b).

HCF vs LCM Magnitude

The **HCF** is always less than or equal to the **LCM**. Specifically, **HCF** ≤ smaller number ≤ larger number ≤ **LCM**.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their **HCF** is 1 and their **LCM** is simply the product of the two numbers.

Divisibility Rule

The **LCM** of a set of numbers is the smallest number that is **divisible** by all the numbers in that set.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will the new bridge open for traffic next week?

options.text: Will the new bridge be opened for traffic next week?
Is the new bridge opened for traffic next week?
Has the new bridge been opened for traffic next week?
Was the new bridge opened for traffic next week?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the new bridge be opened for traffic next week?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Simple Future Tense** (Future Indefinite).
 
• In **Active Voice**, the structure for an interrogative simple future sentence is: **Will/Shall + Subject + Verb (Base Form/V1) + Object?**
 
• To convert this into **Passive Voice**, the structure changes to: **Will/Shall + Object (new subject) + be + Past Participle (V3) + (by + agent)?**
 
• The subject in the active sentence is **the new bridge**, and the main verb is **open**.
 
• When converting to passive, the verb **open** must be changed to its **Past Participle** form, which is **opened**.
 
• Following the rule, the passive construction becomes: **Will** + **the new bridge** + **be** + **opened** + **for traffic next week?**.
 
• This perfectly aligns with the grammatical requirements for maintaining the **future timeline** and the **interrogative mood**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect because they change the **tense** of the original sentence:
 
 
• **Is the new bridge opened...** represents the **Simple Present Passive**, which is used for facts or habitual actions, not future intentions.
 
• **Has the new bridge been opened...** represents the **Present Perfect Passive**, which denotes an action completed in the immediate past.
 
• **Was the new bridge opened...** represents the **Simple Past Passive**, which refers to an action that occurred at a specific time in the past.
 
 
 
• The **auxiliary verb** (will) must remain consistent with the **future time marker** (next week) provided in the context.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

options.text: Do the mentors provide proper guidance to all newly admitted students?

Will the mentors provide proper guidance to all newly admitted students?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Do the mentors provide proper guidance to all newly admitted students?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the **Interrogative Form** of the **Simple Present Tense**. The structure used is **Is/Am/Are + Object + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.

• To convert this into **Active Voice**, the **Object** of the passive sentence (the mentors) must become the **Subject** of the active sentence, and the **Subject** of the passive sentence (proper guidance) must become the **Object**.

• In the **Simple Present Tense**, the interrogative active structure is **Do/Does + Subject + V1 (Base Form) + Object**. Since the new subject **'the mentors'** is plural, the auxiliary verb **'Do'** is required.

• The main verb **'provided'** (V3) is converted back to its base form, **'provide'** (V1), to satisfy the grammatical requirements of the **Active Voice** in this tense.

• The remaining prepositional phrase **'to all newly admitted students'** remains unchanged and is placed at the end of the clause to maintain the original meaning.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Rules for Voice Change across Tenses:**

• **Simple Past Tense:** The active form uses **'Did'** while the passive uses **'Was/Were + V3'**. For example, **'Did they provide guidance?'** becomes **'Was guidance provided by them?'**

• **Present Perfect Tense:** The active form uses **'Has/Have + V3'** while the passive uses **'Has/Have + been + V3'**. This explains why the option starting with **'Have'** is incorrect for a simple present passive sentence.

• **Simple Future Tense:** The active form uses **'Will + V1'** while the passive uses **'Will + be + V3'**. This distinguishes the **Future Tense** from the **Simple Present Tense** used in the question.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** It is critical to match the auxiliary verb (Do/Does) with the number of the subject. **'Do'** is used with **I, You, We, They** and plural nouns, whereas **'Does'** is used with **He, She, It** and singular nouns.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
The reforms were introduced with the hope that they would catalyse an atmosphere conducive of innovation and inclusivity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**conducive to innovation or inclusivity**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The primary error in the original sentence lies in the **prepositional collocation**. In standard English, the adjective **conducive** is strictly followed by the preposition **to** when indicating that a situation or environment makes a particular outcome likely.

• The phrase **conducive of** is considered non-standard or archaic in modern usage; therefore, the replacement must utilize the **to-infinitive** structure or a prepositional phrase starting with **to**.

• The sentence requires **parallelism**, a grammatical principle where items in a series must share the same grammatical form. In the correct option, **innovation** and **inclusivity** are both **abstract nouns**, maintaining the logical balance of the sentence.

• While the original sentence used the conjunction **and**, the option **conducive to innovation or inclusivity** is the only one that corrects the fundamental idiomatic error while preserving the **noun-noun** parallel structure.

• In the context of **economic and social reforms**, creating an atmosphere that is **conducive to** progress is a common **idiomatic expression** used to describe facilitating growth or development.

 **Additional Information__**

• Analysis of Incorrect Options:

• **conducive of innovations with inclusiveness**: This option fails because it retains the incorrect preposition **of** and changes the meaning by using **with**, which does not effectively link the two goals to the atmosphere being created.

• **conducive to innovate and inclusivity**: This choice violates the **rule of parallelism**. It attempts to pair the **verb** **innovate** with the **noun** **inclusivity**. For a sentence to be grammatically sound, both elements linked by **and** or **or** should be of the same **part of speech** (i.e., both nouns).

• **No improvement required**: This is incorrect because the original phrase **conducive of** is a **grammatical error** that must be corrected to **conducive to**.

• Key Definitions:

• **Innovation**: The practical implementation of ideas that result in the introduction of new goods or services or improvement in offering goods or services.

• **Inclusivity**: The policy or practice of providing equal access to opportunities and resources for people who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized.

</ul
